components.title: AWS Elastic Container Registry (ECR)
components.description: Private ECR repositories managed via Terraform (AWS/ECS/modules/ecr/): the Rails application image ({project}-{env}) and the NGINX reverse proxy sidecar ({project}-{env}-nginx), plus two org-adopted standalone-app repositories — vulcan and heimdall2 (unprefixed; published by example-org/container-build-sign, #387). All have scan-on-push, lifecycle policies, AES-256 encryption, and immutable tags. <!-- UPDATE: Insert ECR repository URLs and ARNs for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for ECR

implemented-requirements.description: Malicious Code Protection: ECR scan-on-push is enabled (scan_on_push = true) on every managed repository — the application image, the NGINX sidecar, and the adopted vulcan and heimdall2 repos — automatically scanning each pushed image for known CVEs using the Amazon Inspector scanning engine. Scan findings are available via the ECR console and API, enabling CI/CD pipelines to gate deployments on vulnerability severity. Each image is scanned independently. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000277, CIS AWS 2.1.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: aws_ecr_repository.main (app), aws_ecr_repository.nginx (sidecar), aws_ecr_repository.vulcan, aws_ecr_repository.heimdall2 — all with image_scanning_configuration.scan_on_push = true. vulcan/heimdall2 were pre-existing MUTABLE/no-scan repos brought under management and hardened in #387.

implemented-requirements.description: Baseline Configuration: Image tag immutability is set to IMMUTABLE on every managed repository (app, NGINX sidecar, vulcan, heimdall2), preventing tags from being overwritten. This ensures a given image tag always refers to the same artifact — underpinning the digest-pin / cosign-signature provenance the deploy path relies on. Lifecycle policies on each repo retain the last N images, creating a traceable image history. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000133.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: aws_ecr_repository.main, .nginx, .vulcan, .heimdall2 — all with image_tag_mutability = IMMUTABLE and a lifecycle policy. vulcan/heimdall2 were flipped MUTABLE→IMMUTABLE in place (not ForceNew) when imported in #387.

implemented-requirements.description: Protection of Information at Rest: ECR repositories use AES-256 server-side encryption for all stored images. Container layers and manifests are encrypted at rest in the AWS-managed storage backend. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000231.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resource: aws_ecr_repository.main with encryption_configuration.encryption_type = AES256. Consider KMS CMK for additional control.

implemented-requirements.description: Access Enforcement: ECR repository access is controlled via IAM policies. Only the ECS task execution role has permission to pull images (via AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy). Push access should be restricted to CI/CD pipeline roles. No public access is configured. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000033.
implemented-requirements.remarks: ECR is a private repository. Image pull is authorized via the ECS execution role. Configure repository policies to restrict push access.

implemented-requirements.description: Flaw Remediation: Scan-on-push findings highlight known vulnerabilities in container images, enabling remediation before or during deployment. The lifecycle policy automatically expires old images, reducing the attack surface from unpatched historical versions. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000456.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Integrate ECR scan findings with CI/CD pipelines to prevent deployment of images with critical/high vulnerabilities.
